tema: Explores whether orthostatic chronotropic incompetence exists during the tilt test in ME/CFS patients.
diseno: Retrospective study of a tilt test database with Doppler (stroke volume index supine and at the end); ME/CFS patients and healthy controls without POTS or hypotension; 95% prediction intervals derived from controls. Sample size not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: Supine, the heart rate-stroke volume relationship was similar between groups; during the test, patients had a lower heart rate for a given stroke volume and 37% showed an insufficient increase. It was more frequent in more severe patients.
conclusion: It is the first description of orthostatic chronotropic incompetence in ME/CFS, also relevant for post-COVID-19 patients.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions add the connection with post-COVID. Part of the abstract's results appears truncated.

tema: Characterizes orthostatic intolerance in CFS and studies the effect of exercise on it.
diseno: Study (registered on ClinicalTrials.gov) with 39 CFS patients and 25 controls; symptoms supine and standing with the Gracely Box scale before and after submaximal exercise; POTS and START phenotype (transient post-exertional tachycardia).
hallazgos: Dizziness and lightheadedness were present in 41% of patients supine and 72% standing. Orthostatic tachycardia did not explain the symptoms; there was POTS in 6 and START in 10 patients. ROC analysis stratified patients into no OI, postural OI and persistent OI.
conclusion: Dizziness while supine is underdiagnosed in CFS and should be measured; postural tachycardia and orthostatic symptoms could be separate comorbidities.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on OI, dizziness and POTS; the conclusions add the idea of separate comorbidities. The physical activity keyword refers to submaximal exercise as a challenge, not as a therapeutic intervention.

tema: Patient toolkit intended to avoid PEM (crashes) through prevention plans and trigger monitoring.
diseno: Popular patient document (2017 draft); not a study. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Lists causes of PEM (physical, mental and emotional overexertion, sleep, diet), barriers to avoiding it (lack of warning, support, social and economic pressure) and strategies (planning the day, pacing, knowing one's own patterns, support network).
conclusion: No formal conclusion is stated; the document proposes that reducing PEM can improve baseline functioning and offers a template for an avoidance plan.
triangulacion: Only the opening text of the document is available; there are no keywords or conclusions, so triangulation is not possible.

tema: Compares physical activity and sleep duration between CFS, fibromyalgia and controls and their association with symptom severity in the LifeLines cohort.
diseno: Population-based cross-sectional study (LifeLines): 943 with CFS, 2714 with fibromyalgia and 87,532 controls; questionnaires; adjusted ANCOVA and regression.
hallazgos: CFS and fibromyalgia had lower physical activity than controls; CFS slept more. Only in controls was there a linear association; in all groups there were quadratic associations: low and high levels of activity and short or long sleep were associated with more symptoms.
conclusion: Patients with CFS or fibromyalgia sleep more and are less active; the heterogeneity suggests the importance of patient-tailored treatment.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The diagnosis is self-reported in a general cohort; the conclusions add the idea of aetiological heterogeneity.

tema: Quantifies the pain component of PEM after standardized aerobic exercise in ME/CFS and fibromyalgia.
diseno: Systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of case-control studies: 45 effects from 15 studies with 306 patients and 292 controls; meta-regression.
hallazgos: A small to moderate effect of greater pain after exercise was observed in patients (d=0.42); the effect was larger when pain was measured 8-72 h later (d=0.71) than at 0-2 h (d=0.32).
conclusion: People with ME/CFS and fibromyalgia suffer small to moderate increases in pain after exercise, which confirms pain as a component of PEM.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are fully consistent; the conclusions reproduce the abstract and stress the need to study mechanisms and prescriptions that minimize exacerbation.

tema: Proposes and evaluates postural imbalance as a cause of orthostatic intolerance in ME.
diseno: Study with 72 ME patients (18 men, 54 women); neurological examination (instability with feet together and eyes closed) and 10-min standing test.
hallazgos: Imbalance was present in 32% and orthostatic tachycardia in 22%. Imbalance was much more frequent in those who did not complete the test (89% vs 11%), whereas orthostatic tachycardia did not differ between groups.
conclusion: Imbalance and dysfunction of postural reflexes are strongly associated with OI, and the authors consider them causal and more relevant than orthostatic tachycardia.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions are more forceful than the abstract in asserting causality from observational data.

tema: Examines whether parasympathetic activity (HRV) during deep sleep is reduced in CFS and its relationship to unrefreshing sleep and self-reported wellbeing.
diseno: Case-control study with simultaneous nocturnal EEG and HRV in CFS patients and healthy controls; sample size not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: Unrefreshing sleep and poorer self-reported wellbeing were associated with lower parasympathetic activity during deep sleep (NREM2 and slow-wave sleep), but not in resting wakefulness; total sleep time and the proportion of stages did not explain unrefreshing sleep.
conclusion: The findings support an underlying nocturnal autonomic hypervigilance in the core symptom of CFS, although longitudinal and experimental studies are required to establish causality.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the 'abstract' is a brief summary of rationale and impact without methodological data, and the PDF conclusions add that sleep architecture does not differ.

tema: Historical review of the causal controversy over ME/CFS and the resistance of psychological dogma.
diseno: Narrative review based on the experience of two clinicians; no systematic methodology.
hallazgos: Argues that, as in other historical phenomena, the psychological dogma about the cause of ME/CFS resists being replaced by scientific evidence; mentions a biomarker under development and similarities with long COVID.
conclusion: Scientific research on physical causes will replace psychological dogma; hopes that funds for long COVID will be directed toward finding the pathology and not toward a 'PACE 2'.
triangulacion: Keywords (scientific controversy, history), abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions (from the discussion) are more polemical and add the biomarker and long COVID.

tema: Proposes a pathophysiological model of ME/CFS and possible interventions, centred on an autoimmune mechanism variant that would alter blood flow regulation.
diseno: Perspective article with a pathomechanistic model based on previous literature (autonomic dysfunction, energy metabolism, B cell depletion therapy). No sample stated.
hallazgos: Interprets autonomic dysfunction and increased sympathetic tone as compensatory adaptations to inefficient flow regulation during exertion, and the metabolic changes (altered PDH, use of amino acids and fatty acids) as a response to tissue hypoxia. Suggests an autoimmune variant without tissue inflammation or complement activation.
conclusion: The model is compatible with the absence of histological inflammation and organ damage and with the possibility of recovery; future research should focus on the natural course of the disease.
triangulacion: The available abstract is only a patent declaration on B cell depletion, so the information comes almost exclusively from the PDF conclusions; the keywords (pathogenesis, B cell depletion) are consistent but sparse.

tema: Explains the mechanisms of skeletal muscle energy impairment in ME/CFS and integrates them with the earlier hypothesis of β2-adrenergic receptor dysfunction.
diseno: Hypothesis article without own empirical data.
hallazgos: It is proposed that β2AdR dysfunction insufficiently stimulates the Na+/K+-ATPase, causing sodium overload that reverses the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger and causes calcium overload with mitochondrial, metabolic and endothelial damage; the upregulated NHE1 would lower the threshold for re-induction even with everyday activities.
conclusion: This vicious circle would explain PEM, exercise intolerance and chronification; dysfunctions of β2AdR, NHE1, Na+/K+-ATPase, NCX, RAAS and the kallikrein-kinin system should be investigated as possible therapeutic targets.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent around sympatholysis and sodium overload; the discussion (with acknowledgement noise) broadens the targets to RAAS and kallikrein-kinin and acknowledges predispositions that are still unknown.

tema: Delineates the protein-protein interaction network of chronic fatigue spectrum disorders (including ME/CFS) and the pathways enriched in it.
diseno: Bioinformatic network, enrichment and annotation analysis from differentially expressed proteins and metabolites described in CFAS-D patients; no own sample.
hallazgos: The network core includes NFKB1, CTNNB1, ALB, peroxides, NOS2, TNF and IL-6, with interconnected immuno-oxidative-nitrosative and Wnt/β-catenin subnetworks. The network is associated with antioxidant detoxification, hydrogen peroxide metabolism, IL-10 signalling, canonical Wnt, cell junctions, TLR2/4 and NF-κB/RELA pathways, and responses to toxins, LPS, bacteria or viruses.
conclusion: CFAS-D could be triggered by various stimuli whose effects would be mediated by alterations in the interaction between redox, NF-κB and Wnt/β-catenin pathways; this interaction could constitute a new therapeutic target.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on PPI networks and redox, NF-κB and Wnt signalling; the PDF conclusions broaden toward bacterial translocation with LPS as a possible trigger and toward therapeutic strategies not evaluated in the study.

tema: Identifies the infectious diseases self-reported by patients as triggers of ME/CFS onset.
diseno: International multicentre study with 1773 people diagnosed with ME, CFS or ME/CFS; coding and classification of self-reported qualitative data on infectious triggers.
hallazgos: 60.3% reported some infectious illness before onset; the most frequent was mononucleosis (30% of infections), but more than 100 different infectious diseases were mentioned.
conclusion: Many different infectious agents could be associated with ME/CFS onset; the study is exploratory and should serve as a starting point for longitudinal and quasi-experimental designs.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion agree on the diversity of infectious triggers; the discussion is more cautious, warns that the remaining 39.7% may have had asymptomatic infections and limits the conclusions to self-report.

tema: Checks whether CFS patients have reduced absolute cerebral blood flow.
diseno: Xenon CT in 25 CFS patients and 7 healthy controls, with stratification according to the presence of a current psychiatric disorder.
hallazgos: Patients without a psychiatric disorder had lower cortical flow in the territories of both middle cerebral arteries, and those with a psychiatric disorder only on the left (P < 0.05).
conclusion: CFS patients have lower absolute cortical flow, more extensive in those without psychopathology, which supports that part of the symptoms is due to brain dysfunction; more controls are needed.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree; the conclusions (from the discussion, with table data) are more cautious in warning of higher control values than in previous studies.

tema: Presents the Munich Berlin Symptom Questionnaires (MBSQ) for diagnosing ME/CFS after COVID-19 in paediatric and adult patients.
diseno: Series of 10 patients aged 11 to 25 from a chronic fatigue centre for young people, evaluated with the MBSQ, scoring sheets and validated PROMs.
hallazgos: All 10 patients were diagnosed with ME/CFS after asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection or mild-moderate COVID-19, with severe limitations in daily activities and quality of life.
conclusion: ME/CFS can follow SARS-CoV-2 infection in those under 18; the MBSQ are new tools to facilitate structured diagnosis.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions come from the abstract itself, so they provide no independent information.

tema: Proposes persistent fatigue induced by interferon alpha (IFN-α) in hepatitis C patients as an inflammatory model of CFS to study immunity before, during and after the trigger.
diseno: Prospective cohort of 55 HCV patients treated with IFN-α evaluated at baseline, during 6-12 months of treatment and 6 months after; comparison with 54 CFS patients and 57 healthy volunteers; measurement of fatigue, cytokines and kynurenine pathway metabolites.
hallazgos: 33% developed persistent fatigue; these patients had a greater increase in fatigue in the first 4 weeks, higher baseline IL-10 and a tendency toward higher IL-6, with levels more than double at week 4. There was no peripheral inflammation at 6 months or in the CFS cohort; CFS patients had a lower kynurenine/tryptophan ratio and 3-hydroxykynurenine.
conclusion: No explicit conclusion is stated in the available sources; the abstract suggests that an exaggerated immune response to the trigger, rather than sustained inflammation, is associated with persistent fatigue.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (IFN-α, cytokines, IL-6). The conclusions text comes from the discussion but only contains conflicts of interest, funding and supplementary material, and the abstract appears truncated, so the formal conclusion is missing.

tema: Evaluates whether AMPK can be pharmacologically activated in skeletal muscle cultures from ME/CFS patients.
diseno: In vitro study with primary muscle cell cultures from ME/CFS patients and controls treated with metformin or compound 991; AMPK Western blot, glucose uptake and ATP content. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Metformin and 991 significantly increased AMPK activation and glucose uptake in both groups. Cellular ATP did not change with treatment, but was significantly lower in ME/CFS.
conclusion: Pharmacological activation of AMPK improves glucose uptake, suggesting a defect proximal to AMPK in the response to electrical stimulation; whether it improves muscle function in patients remains to be determined.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the discussion, with funding and abbreviation noise) are fully consistent on AMPK, glucose and reduced ATP.

tema: Pilot study describing, by transmission electron microscopy, the morphology and ultrastructure of peripheral immune cells in ME/CFS.
diseno: Pilot study with PBMC from four participants: identical twins discordant for moderate ME/CFS, one patient with an extremely severe form and one healthy control; TEM of unstimulated and CD3/CD28-stimulated cells.
hallazgos: The patients' stimulated T cells showed more than double the cell death by apoptosis and necrosis and more swollen mitochondria. The extremely severe patient showed a large increase in giant lipid-droplet-like organelles, and a slight increase in platelet aggregation was observed.
conclusion: There are extensive morphological alterations in immune cells and mitochondria; despite the small sample, the increase in apoptosis and necrosis and the relationship between mitochondrial swelling and severity require replication in larger cohorts.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions are consistent on apoptosis, necrosis, mitochondria and lipid droplets; the conclusions acknowledge the small sample size and add an emphasis on genetic and epigenetic factors not developed in the abstract.

tema: Compares three measures of physical activity in ME/CFS: the SF-36 physical function scale, daily steps with an actimeter and % peak VO2 on CPET.
diseno: Retrospective clinical database study with 99 women with ME/CFS with the three measures within an interval of 3 months or less; linear regression; 20 reassessed because of worsening.
hallazgos: The three measures correlated linearly and positively, with no differences according to fibromyalgia or maximal effort; in the 20 reassessed, all three decreased. There was great individual variation between measures.
conclusion: Given the individual variation, a single measure is insufficient; integrating the three can detect discrepancies and guide care and studies.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions add the possible over- or underestimation of perceived activity and the need to study energy management.

tema: Evaluates the test-retest reliability and clinically significant change of the two-day CPET in Gulf War illness (GWI).
diseno: Study with 15 veterans with GWI and 8 controls (after excluding 15 without peak effort); ICC, smallest real difference (SRD%) and repeated-measures ANOVA at VAT and peak.
hallazgos: ICCs at peak were moderate to excellent in GWI (mean 0.84) and lower at VAT (0.68); the SRD% was lower at peak (18.8) than at VAT (28.1). There were no significant group-time interactions.
conclusion: A framework is provided for evaluating the reliability of the two-day CPET; PEM studies must consider measurement error to avoid false positives.
triangulacion: The three sources agree; the focus is methodological and on GWI, not directly on ME/CFS. The conclusions are cautious and warn about the interpretation of changes in ME/CFS.

tema: Studies the relationship between end-tidal CO2 and cerebral blood flow during orthostatic stress in ME/CFS and controls.
diseno: Retrospective study in 535 women with ME/CFS (normal haemodynamic response or POTS) and 34 healthy controls; CBF by extracranial Doppler and PETCO2 supine and at the end of the tilt test; multiple regression.
hallazgos: There was a significant relationship between CBF and PETCO2 in patients, with no differences between normal response and POTS; the relationship between CBF change and PETCO2 decrease was significant in both groups, but with low adjusted R2.
conclusion: In women with ME/CFS, CO2 reactivity is similar to that of controls and independent of the haemodynamic pattern, although it depends on age and severity; the influence of CO2 on CBF is modest.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add the dependence on age and severity and note as a limitation that only women were studied. The conclusions section contains editorial noise.

tema: Evaluates the physiological response of ME/CFS patients to a 10-minute passive tilt test with capnography.
diseno: Longitudinal study with 63 consecutive patients (1994 criteria) evaluated in 1 to 3 annual visits (48 and 29 at visits 2 and 3); respiratory and heart rate, blood pressure and eTCO2, plus questionnaires on symptoms, quality of life and mood.
hallazgos: 60.3% showed some abnormality at some visit. Hypocapnia, at rest or induced, was the most frequent and persistent, ahead of orthostatic tachycardia; anxiety did not differ according to hypocapnia.
conclusion: The 10-min tilt test is useful for evaluating OI in ME/CFS, and hypocapnia would go unnoticed without capnography; its correlation with symptoms and its usefulness for monitoring treatment remain to be determined.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on hypocapnia and OI; the discussion, with declaration noise, is more cautious and calls for studies of correlation with symptoms and therapeutic response.

tema: Validates the presence of innate immune activation and platelet dense granule deficiency in POTS.
diseno: Case-control study: 35 POTS patients and 35 non-POTS subjects with unexplained bleeding symptoms; 16 cytokines and chemokines by multiplex flow cytometry and electron microscopy of dense granules.
hallazgos: Ten of 16 inflammatory biomarkers were elevated in POTS, with increased IL-1β and IL-18 and normal or low type 1 interferons. All POTS patients had delta granule deficiency.
conclusion: POTS would show a mixed inflammatory pattern, with autoinflammatory and possibly T cell-mediated autoimmunity features, which is being studied prospectively.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions are somewhat more nuanced than the abstract in raising T autoimmunity as a hypothesis under study and highlighting the mixed pattern.

tema: Examines whether poliomyelitis vaccination affects CFS patients and whether they excrete more virus, as a test of susceptibility to enterovirus.
diseno: Trial with 18 CFS patients randomly assigned to polio vaccine or placebo and 9 vaccinated healthy volunteers, controlling for recent booster vaccination.
hallazgos: Vaccination had no negative effects in the CFS group. Viral excretion was greater in vaccinated patients than in vaccinated controls, but the difference was not significant.
conclusion: Polio vaccination is not contraindicated in CFS patients, but a greater susceptibility to enterovirus infection could not be confirmed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions explicitly stress that the greater viral excretion of the earlier study was not replicated, which qualifies the enteroviral hypothesis suggested by the keywords.

tema: Reviews the emerging role of polyphenols as alternative agents in chronic fatigue and CFS based on preclinical and clinical studies.
diseno: Narrative review of in vitro, in vivo and clinical studies. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Numerous polyphenols (flavonoids, resveratrol, curcumin) showed promising results in chronic fatigue models, mainly by counteracting oxidative stress and inflammation; clinical data are very limited.
conclusion: Randomized placebo-controlled trials, focused on dose and duration, are needed before considering clinical use; bioavailability is an important limitation.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions add the limitation of bioaccessibility and bioavailability, not mentioned in the abstract.

tema: Evaluates the effect of a multi-strain probiotic on fatigue, depression and quality of life in post-infectious fatigue.
diseno: Double-blind placebo-controlled pilot trial in 70 patients with post-infectious fatigue; FSS, BDI-II and SF-36 at baseline, 3 and 6 months; laboratory parameters and tryptophan and phenylalanine metabolism.
hallazgos: Both groups improved, but the probiotic group had significantly lower FSS and BDI-II at 6 months (p<0.001) and improved quality of life, whereas placebo only improved in physical limitation and energy/fatigue. Neopterin was higher with placebo; there were no changes in interferon gamma-mediated pathways.
conclusion: Probiotics could be a promising intervention in post-infectious fatigue, possibly through modulation of the gut-brain axis.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent. The conclusions text is almost all noise (contributions, funding); it is notable that the medication was supplied by the manufacturing company. Important placebo effect.
